On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. # Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

20	## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
21	User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

23	## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
24	- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
25	- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
26	- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
27	- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

14	## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
15	- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
16	- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
17	- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
18	- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). ### D.10 Hash and canonical bytes

The layout hash formula is defined as:

`geometry_hash = low32( H64( canonical_geometry_bytes ) )` · `visual_hash = low32( H64( canonical_visual_bytes ) )` (the two halves of the former `template_hash`, LY-26 e; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*) · `layout_hash = block_hash(&"layout.state") = H64( canonical_bytes( layout.state snapshot ) )` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)*. `canonical_bytes` is the kernel's prefix-free TLV form (kernel D.12); Layout owns the snapshot SHAPE only (the AC-130 allow-list, arrays in ascending id order, tombstones retained, derived caches `version`, grids, leaf cache, PROJECTOR objects and `mutation_count` excluded) and writes no byte encoder for the block. `layout_hash()` calls the kernel read `block_hash(&"layout.state", uncached = true)` (new, kernel request K-2), which exists in every build because Horror HE-25 keys its path cache on it in release. The two template-local byte strings `canonical_geometry_bytes` and `canonical_visual_bytes` (and only those) are `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` per field in a fixed documented order (ADR-LAY-06); they are never compared with a kernel value

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `H64` | function | 64-bit | the kernel's H64 (kernel D.12 and Tuning Knobs `H64`/`mix64` row; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling X13 / R-17): the first 8 bytes, little-endian, of SHA-256 computed with Godot's `HashingContext`; native, no GDScript byte loop *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* | one hash for the whole project |
| `canonical_geometry_bytes` | bytes | template-sized | template | rooms by `room_key` with `origin_px` and tile runs, rects in D.9 order, socket and door positions, hardpoint cells, anchor polylines; strings as length-prefixed UTF-8 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `canonical_visual_bytes` | bytes | small | template | kit-piece ids, art references, dialect, labels *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `canonical_bytes( layout.state )` | bytes | tens of bytes to tens of KB | the kernel's TLV encoder (kernel D.12) over the block snapshot | counters, bodies, instances, sockets, welds; Layout supplies the snapshot shape only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* |
| `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` | u32 each | `[0, 2^32)` | persisted per instance | drift gate (LY-26 e) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| hash cadence | policy | n/a | this GDD | see Output Range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

**Output Range:** `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash` are u32, `layout_hash` is u64 and travels as two int32 halves in the payload (hex only in Save/Load's header, SL-2 S-1); none is ever emitted as a JSON number. The kernel's `state_hash` (kernel D.12) consumes `layout_hash` unchanged. **Cadence** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the kernel's GDScript canonical-bytes encode of the block plus the native SHA-256 is not free (kernel D.12 'Cost': dominated by the encoder, not by H64; [UNV], spike SP-ENG-1 P5), so `layout_hash` is **never computed per tick**: it is computed (i) when Save/Load captures the block, (ii) once after `restore()`/`post_restore()` and compared with the value **stored by its owner, Save/Load's `block_state_hash` for `layout.state` in the slot header (SL-1 `blocks[]`, SL-16; optional: written in dev/test captures, absent from a release capture, in which case no comparison is made; Save/Load owns the stored copy and `layout.state` holds no `layout_hash` field, which is why the AC-130 allow-list has none)**; this value is the kernel's `block_hash` of the same block, so equality is exact (AC-181) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* (a mismatch is a diagnostic, not a restore reason, because the kernel owns `state_hash` verification), (iii) in debug builds at the kernel's `state_hash` cadence, and (iv) on demand by the Debug Overlay; the result is memoised on a block `mutation_count` bumped by LM1-LM4, so a repeat call with no mutation costs O(1). **`mutation_count` is a non-persisted, non-hashed derived cache** (it is in no LY-2 table, in no snapshot and in no canonical byte), **reset to 0 by `restore()` with the memo invalidated**, so two equal blocks built by different histories hash equal (AC-172). `geometry_hash` / `visual_hash` are computed once per template load and cached. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the stored `layout_hash` had no owner and `mutation_count` was undeclared.)* **GDScript integer rules for the hashes** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: GDScript has signed 64-bit `int` only, and `PackedInt32Array` stores signed 32-bit values. A u32 `geometry_hash` / `visual_hash` is therefore **persisted as a signed int32** and **normalised with `& 0xFFFFFFFF` on both sides before every compare** (a stored value read back at or above 2^31 is negative until normalised, and an un-normalised compare would raise a false `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` on about half of all templates); `layout_hash` travels as two int32 halves `(hi, lo)` each normalised the same way. `H64` is the kernel's (see the H64 row). Layout contains no hash loop and no shift-based mixing. Template hashes call the same H64 over the template-local byte strings. A signed 64-bit `h` is split into the int32 halves `hi = (h >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF` and `lo = h & 0xFFFFFFFF` (the mask removes GDScript's arithmetic-shift sign extension), each then stored as a signed int32 and re-normalised with `& 0xFFFFFFFF` before every compare. The Save/Load header hex of a hash is the little-endian digest prefix (hex64, SL F-10), e.g. SHA-256("abc") gives "ba7816bf8f01cfea", never the big-endian hex of the integer. Layout must not call the built-in `hash()`, `Array.hash()` or `Dictionary.hash()` (not stable across builds; scanned by AC-8). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)*

**Example:** the `counters` dictionary `{next_section_id, next_body_id, next_room_id}` encodes in the kernel TLV as 102 bytes = 9 (DICT header: 1 + 8) + 30 (`next_body_id`: key 1 + 8 + 12 = 21, INT 9) + 30 (`next_room_id`: 21 + 9) + 33 (`next_section_id`: key 1 + 8 + 15 = 24, INT 9) — entries sort by encoded key, which orders the u64 length first, so the two 12-character keys come first (`next_body_id` before `next_room_id`) and the 15-character key last; 119 bytes including its own parent key `counters` (1 + 8 + 8 = 17). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* A visual-only template edit changes `visual_hash` but not `geometry_hash` or any key set or tile set, so restore accepts it with one diagnostic. A socket `start_px` or wall-rect edit changes `geometry_hash` with every key set and tile set unchanged: on a welded or otherwise non-`FREE` instance restore refuses it (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`); on a never-welded `FREE` instance it is accepted with `geometry_changed_fresh`. A tile-set edit is refused by the key-set comparison, not by a hash — a 2^−32 collision therefore cannot hide a structural change. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

content.content:
`block_hash(b) = H64( canonical_bytes(b) )` — **cached per block and invalidated by the block's dirty bit** (any write in P2/P3 clears it; `restore` clears it) **for the diagnostics cadence only**: `state_hash(scope, T, uncached = false)` may use the cache; `state_hash(scope, T, uncached = true)` re-encodes every block in scope and ignores it. **Every determinism check — G3, G4, the K-4 verification window (CR-15), the `STRICT_DEBUG` tripwire and the test profile — calls `uncached = true`**, because in 4.7 a packed-array element write skips the setter, so a mutator that forgets `mark_dirty` leaves a stale cached hash and a cached comparison would pass falsely on exactly the bug G4 exists to catch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

**Published read `block_hash(block_id: StringName, uncached: bool = true) -> BlockHashResult`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, request from the Layout re-review)*: available in every build — it is not part of the dev-only `diagnostics` accessor (UI Requirements) — it returns `{ok, hash, reason}`, where `hash` is D.12's `block_hash(b)` for one registered `persist` block as the signed 64-bit pattern of `H64` (print with `hex64`). It is a pure read: the kernel calls the owner's `snapshot(ctx)` with a fresh `ctx` of its own (a deep copy that mutates nothing, CR-8, ending `return ctx.complete()`, CR-19), passes the payload through `canonical_encode` and hashes the bytes. With `uncached = true` it ignores the dirty-bit cache and counts as one `canonical_bytes` encode in the KRN-PERF-01 counter; `uncached = false` may return the cache (diagnostics only). **When it may be called:** in any phase or boundary service except while a `WriteScope` is open on that block (inside a P2 `apply`, or a mutator chain that writes it, where the block may be half-written between two mutator calls of one command): there it returns `ok = false` with reason `BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE`. From P3 onward, in P5 and in a boundary service it is consistent, because hooks run one at a time. A caller memoises on its own mutation counter so the encode runs only after a block mutation, never per tick; Layout's `layout_hash()` reads it, so Layout and Horror's path cache (HE-25) read it from P3 or a boundary, never from inside an `apply`. The value is the one Save/Load stores as `block_state_hash` (SL-16). An unknown `block_id` or a non-`persist` block returns `ok = false` with reason `BLOCK_HASH_UNKNOWN`, never a hash of 0.

**Published encoder `canonical_encode(value) -> PackedByteArray`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, request from Ship Body)*: the TLV form below is the **only** canonical-bytes definition in the project. An owner GDD describes the *shape* of its `snapshot()` payload (keys, value types, row order) and never a byte layout, and no owner ships its own byte writer. The encoder is a pure static helper (no kernel instance needed, not compiled out of release) and is the same function `block_hash` and `state_hash` use, so an owner test can encode a sub-value of its payload (for example Body's `actors` key).

`state_hash(scope, T) = H64( T ‖ world_seed ‖ ⨁_{b ∈ scope, sorted by block_id} ( len(block_id) ‖ block_id ‖ schema_version ‖ len(canonical_bytes(b)) ‖ block_hash(b) ) )`, where `canonical_bytes` is the **prefix-free tag-length-value (TLV) form** below *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the earlier form carried no type tags and no counts, so `[[1],[2,3]]` and `[[1,2],[3]]` collided, an `int` and a `float` with the same bits collided, and `VECTOR2`, `VECTOR2I`, `NIL` and `STRING_NAME` had no encoding)*: every value is **one tag byte followed by a self-delimiting body**, so no encoding is a prefix of another and the map from values to bytes is injective. Tags and bodies — `0x00 NIL` (no body); `0x01 BOOL` (1 byte, 0 or 1); `0x02 INT` (8 bytes, little-endian two's complement); `0x03 FLOAT` (8 bytes, the IEEE-754 bit pattern, little-endian, with `−0.0 → +0.0` and every NaN → `0x7FF8000000000000`); `0x04 STRING` (u64 little-endian UTF-8 byte length, then the bytes) — **a `StringName` is encoded as the `STRING` of its text**, so equal text is equal bytes; `0x05 VECTOR2` (two normalised `FLOAT` bodies, 16 bytes, no inner tags); `0x06 VECTOR2I` (two 8-byte little-endian ints, sign-extended, 16 bytes); `0x07 ARRAY` (u64 element **count**, then that many tagged values, in order); `0x08 DICT` (u64 entry **count**, then `key, value` tagged pairs sorted bytewise by the **encoded key bytes**; all keys of one dictionary share one type, CR-4); `0x09 PACKED` (one element-type byte, u64 element count, then the raw little-endian element bytes; a `PackedStringArray` element is a u64 length plus UTF-8, a `PackedVector2Array` element is two 4-byte floats). Owners keep NaN and `−0.0` out of packed float state — mutators normalise, and a test asserts it. **Worked examples (hand-derived, normative for the encoder tests; `u64(n)` is 8 little-endian bytes)**: `INT 1` = `02 u64(1)`; `FLOAT 1.0` = `03 00 00 00 00 00 00 F0 3F`; `[[1],[2,3]]` = `07 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(1) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(2) 02 u64(3)`, whereas `[[1,2],[3]]` = `07 u64(2) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(1) 02 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(3)` — they differ at the second count, so they cannot collide, and `INT 1` and `FLOAT 1.0` differ at the tag

|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| scope | enum | {`PERSIST` (G4), `ALL_SIM` (G3)} | calculated (test chooses) | `PERSIST` = blocks with `persist = true` **and** `persist_scope = WORLD` — never `PROFILE`; `ALL_SIM` = every `SIM` block (`WORLD`, `PROFILE` and non-persisted derived). Both **exclude `kernel.clock`** (its `T` and `world_seed` are the hash prefix, so they are counted once) and **never include `PERCEPTION_OUT`** |

#### 1.2 Rectangles, walls, frames

**LY-7 — The footprint rectangle record and flags** (registry: `layout_rect_flags`)**.** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, stored as packed integer arrays plus one flags byte, **half-open** `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` over pixel CELLS (the tile grid, the foot box and sprite rows are all cells). Flags: `SOLID` (blocks `LocomotionStep`), `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` (the Emitter's `occludes_light`, EM-20), `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL`. Rects are SIMULATION DATA (kernel H10): never read back from the scene tree, never produced by an engine physics shape, and the avatar has no physics body. Layout never calls its own rects "collision shapes" (wording refresh routed in Cross-References). The only legal flag combinations (anything else is the lint error `RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`):

| Class | SOLID | OCCLUDES_LIGHT | DOOR_LEAF | PROP | MACHINE | HULL | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wall run | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/1 | HULL on exterior-facing runs |
| Door jamb | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | fixed, either side of the gap |
| Door leaf | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | always solid and occluding (no glass in MVP, EM-20); dynamic (LY-9) |
| Socket hatch plate (variant slot PLATE) while `FREE`, `CAPPED`, `CUT_OPEN` or `WELDED` one-sided | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | the plate covers the whole socket span (`width_tiles × 48` × 24); a reserved variant slot, not a static rect (LY-15). While `CUT_OPEN` it is solid AND occluding: nothing lies beyond a cut, and no avatar can leave the hull through it. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Socket jamb (variant slot JAMB), `WELDED` two-sided, `width_tiles >= 3` only | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | the hull bulkhead beside the 96-px hatch doorway, `(width_tiles × 48 − 96)` × 24; exterior hull wall, hence HULL; zero-width (omitted) at `width_tiles` 2. Same precedent as the hull-port row below: the HULL run compiles in parts with no SOLID overlap. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Tall prop / machinery node | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0/1 | 0 | `occludes_light` authored |
| Low prop | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | blocks feet, not light |
| Hull port (`wall_port` piece in a HULL run; routed from Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-19 / OQ-V2) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | blocks feet, passes light, so a residual lamp's light truthfully leaves the hull; its footprint replaces the HULL run's own over its span (the run compiles in two parts, no SOLID overlap) and `CONTAINMENT_LEAK` is unaffected because it is SOLID; it is absent from `rects_in`, not a translucent occluder, so EM-20 (f) is untouched |

Two query filters, never merged: `solid_in(body_id, aabb)` returns SOLID rects (Body's sweep); `OccluderSource.rects_in(aabb)` returns OCCLUDES_LIGHT rects (Emitter, Lighting). A rect with `x1 <= x0` or `y1 <= y0` is **omitted from every result** but keeps its reserved `idx`, so a fully open leaf renumbers nothing; the omission itself bumps `leaf_version` (and so `version`, LY-12 d). The same omission rule governs the socket variant slots (PLATE, JAMB; LY-15): a slot that is inactive in the socket's current state, or whose computed length is zero, is omitted from every result and keeps its reserved `idx`, so a weld, a cut or a restore never adds or removes a key from the reserved set `(section_id, idx)` — only the active subset changes. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(CLARIFY, orchestrator ruling: the DOOR_LEAF exemption.)* The 24-grid rule has one exception: a leaf's fixed axes lie on the 24 grid but its moving edge takes any integer in `[hinge, hinge + width_px]` (LY-9). The broadphase (LY-12) therefore stores static rects only; leaves (and the socket variant slots, which change only inside LM2 and LM3 and are rebuilt into the grid there) live in a small per-section dynamic list tested with a bounding-box prefilter, because re-inserting a moving rect into a uniform grid every tick costs more than testing a handful of boxes.

**LY-8 — Walls, corners, canonical decomposition, corridors, doorways, floor runs.**
(a) *Depth.* A wall footprint is `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 thick normal to its run in BOTH orientations (an E-W wall: 24 rows deep, the run wide; a N-S wall: 24 columns wide, the run tall). Corner cells belong to the E-W run; N-S runs are trimmed to exclude the 24×24 corner, so the compiled table has no overlapping duplicates ("corners are the union").
(b) *Which half-tile.* Which half-tile of a 48×96 kit piece the footprint occupies is the kit piece's authored rect, not a Layout formula (PIPE:794 routes the projection convention to the art-director); Layout lints alignment (every coordinate on the 24 grid) and derives `sort_origin_y = y_0 + 24` per Pipeline D.12 (cited, not restated). The first legal row south of a wall with rows `[y_0, y_0 + 24)` is `y_0 + 24` (the rect is occupied through `y_0 + 23`, LY-12).
(c) *Canonical order.* Within a template, `idx` is assigned by sorting all rects by `(y0, x0, y1, x1, flags)` at load; no two SOLID rects of one template may overlap (lint `RECT_OVERLAP`; abutting is legal). Door-leaf rects are indexed by their door's declaration order and keep that index while their coordinates change. Consequence: the key `(section_id, idx)` is stable across attach, detach and animation.

**LY-1 — One block, one ownership clause.** Layout registers exactly one state block, `layout.state` (registry: `layout_state_block`), in the kernel's block registry (CR-8):

| Field | Value | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | `layout.state` | Layout |
| `owner` | Layout | Layout |
| `class` | `SIM` | Layout |
| `persist` / `persist_scope` | true / `WORLD` | Layout |
| `scope` | `SHARED` | Layout |
| `repl_hint` | `SHARED_SUMMARY` — the summary IS the instance table plus the `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash` values *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the single `template_hash` is split, LY-26 e)*; geometry never travels, because templates are identical on every client by catalogue version | Layout |
| `schema_version` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1 | Layout |
2:- **(a) Fault channel and the one callable contract** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3; defines the contract once)*. **Kernel-invoked owner callables** are a closed list: `validate`, `apply`, step hooks, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `read_view`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline`, `init_world`, and the result- and subscriber-handlers. The kernel calls each through `Callable.call()` and passes a context object as the last argument (`ApplyContext`/`WriteScope`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `NotifyContext`). **Results flow through `ctx`, never through the return value**: `validate(cmd, views, ctx)` reports through `ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)`; `snapshot(ctx)`, `default_state(ctx)` and `read_view(ctx)` deliver their payload through `ctx.put(payload)`; `apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, hooks, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` and handlers report only success-by-completion; every callable reports failure with `ctx.fault(code, detail)`. **Every callable's only return statement is `return ctx.complete()`** (a typed token, (b)); no owner callable is declared `-> void`, because a `void` GDScript function cannot return the token and the engine's default for an aborted typed function would alias a legitimate result. A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`; the first outcome call stands and a second is a violation (`CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`). **Published mutators are not on this list**: other owners, not the kernel, call them, so the kernel cannot check their sentinel; they take the shared `WriteScope`, report with `scope.fault(code, detail)` and return a status that callers propagate — which is also why the sentinel's blind spot (below) is closed by status propagation. The kernel checks `ctx.faulted` (which includes any fault a mutator reported on the shared scope) and the completion token after **every** kernel-invoked call, before using its result. A fault in `apply`, a hook, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `default_state`, `commit_baseline` or `snap_baseline` (and in a mutator they called) moves the kernel to `FAULTED`; **a fault in `read_view` never does**: views are obtained by presentation at render time, outside any tick, and a HUD read must not be able to halt the ship (CR-11, H4) — it is recorded and counted (`INCOMPLETE` or the violation, as a P5 handler's is), the reader receives an empty view, and w
3:- **(b) Completion sentinel.** The kernel arms `ctx.completed = false` and a fresh `ctx.token` before each call; `ctx.complete()` sets `completed` and returns that token — a typed, non-nil, non-zero object (a per-call `CompletionToken` instance) that the kernel compares **by identity**, so a `null`, `0`, `false` or empty value returned by an aborted or forgetful function can never read as success. A call that returns anything but the armed token with `completed` set (the script aborted on an engine error, or forgot) is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` for `apply`, hooks, `validate`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` and `init_world`, and a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic, without a fault, for a P5 or result handler and for `read_view` (which returns an empty view). In a release build the sentinel is the only abort guard (`assert` is compiled out), so it is exercised on a release export in the spike (Acceptance Criteria, KRN-CTX-06). The sentinel catches a *function that aborted*; it cannot catch an error in a nested helper that the outer function then ignores — which is why mutators also return statuses and callers must propagate them.
4:- **(c) What cannot be done.** Engine script errors cannot be intercepted. P5 subscriber isolation is therefore **best-effort plus lint**: the kernel calls handlers one at a time from its own loop, so an aborted handler does not stop the loop; the sentinel names the offending subscriber in diagnostics; a lint forbids handlers from calling anything that can write.

Layout's `entity_id` (publisher-defined, G1; the namespace tag is registered with the Pipeline, Open Questions OQ-LY-ID):** a block-tagged int64, `entity_id = (LAYOUT_ID_NS << 56) | (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | template_local_idx`, with `LAYOUT_ID_NS` a Layout namespace byte in `1 … 127` (GDScript `int` is signed 64-bit, so a byte of 128 or more would make every Layout `entity_id` negative; the Pipeline compares ids as plain ints and only relative order inside one namespace matters, but the range is fixed so the sign is never in question) that Body, Interaction and any other id publisher must not use in its own high bits (so a Layout id can never equal a Body or Interaction id in the same `class_rank`), `section_id` 32 bits at most (`next_section_id` is monotonic and tombstones keep their ids), `kind_ordinal` 8 bits, `template_local_idx` 16 bits. It is a pure function of the block (`section_id`) and the template, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one, and it is never persisted by the PROJECTOR. **Tiles carry no `entity_id`:** `TileMapLayer` cells are not nodes; wall-face and cap tiles are `class_rank` 0 and tie-break among themselves by cell position `(y, x)` (the engine's own order for a `TileMapLayer`, Y-sort mechanism per SP-YSORT-1 below). Within `class_rank` 2 the doors, props and machinery of one `sort_y` are ordered by `entity_id` alone (they share one rank in the Pipeline; Layout assumes no sub-rank). ### D.19 Escape-route budget (Authoring's content lint; Layout supplies `route_length_px`)

The escape-route budget formula is defined as:

`ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX(n, V) = max( 0, ( W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE − ESCAPE_REACTION_TICKS − n × (DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS + 1) ) × V )` with `n >= 1` the number of closable doors the route must close (the single-door budget is `n = 1`, `V = V_RUN`; a carry route uses `V = V_CARRY`, below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the `n` term is inside the formula, so the "n closed doors subtract" sentence no longer double-counts the one door the formula already includes; the `max(0, …)` floor stops the budget going negative when `W_MIN_WARNING_S` is 4 s or less; the raw value `<= 0` raises Authoring's ERROR lint `ESCAPE_BUDGET_NONPOSITIVE`, a proposed id routed to Derelict Authoring, and the Manhattan route length makes the lint conservative: a real route is never shorter than `Manhattan`, AC-115)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE × V_RUN` = 1,800 px spent the whole warning on running, with zero slack for noticing the warning or for the door.)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `W_MIN_WARNING_S` | int (s) | 10 | the Graph (fairness gate, REG:1665) | minimum warning before an endogenous transition |
| `TICK_RATE` | int | 60 | the kernel (REG:1375) | ticks per second |
| `ESCAPE_REACTION_TICKS` | int (ticks) | 60 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (range 30–180) | Derelict Authoring / game-designer (provisional; **not** Attention's `REACT_ALLOW_TICKS` 180, a different quantity — the abortability allowance of a horror tell) | ticks between the warning becoming readable and the player starting to run *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` | int (ticks) | 30 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (range 18–60) | Interaction (registry `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS`, cited) | the uniform door-attempt window before the close lands *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `+ 1` | int (tick) | 1 | the kernel's T+1 command application (the SYSTEM `set_opening` applies in P2 of T+1, IA-24) | the close lands one tick after the window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `V_RUN` | int (px/tick) | 3 | the Controller / Pipeline (REG:1158) | run speed |

**Output Range:** `(600 − 60 − 31) × 3` = **1,527 px** (31.8 tiles; at `V_WALK` 2 the same budget covers 1,018 px). Derived, not new: Layout owns no knob here (`ESCAPE_REACTION_TICKS` is Authoring's, provisional); the lint "every anchor whose descriptor can fail endogenously has a closable door within the budget along `route_length_px`" is Authoring's (Pillar 2 content rule). The figure above is for one closable door (`n = 1`); for a route that must close `n` doors, evaluate the formula with that `n` (it already subtracts `n × (DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS + 1)` ticks, so nothing further is subtracted for the first door). **Floor examples** (recomputed from the formula; the finding's "4 s or less" threshold does not hold at the registry defaults): at `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 1 the raw tick term is `60 − 60 − 31 = −31`, so the budget floors to 0 and `ESCAPE_BUDGET_NONPOSITIVE` fires; at 2 it is `120 − 60 − 31 = 29` ticks (87 px at `V_RUN`); the floor binds earlier with larger `n` (at `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 4, `n` = 5 gives `240 − 60 − 155 = 25` ticks, `n` = 6 gives `−6` and floors to 0). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)*

**Example:** the cryo bay's 336-px crossing is `336 / 3 = 112` ticks, 1.87 s at a run — about 19 % of the warning's 10 s and `336 / 1,527` = 22 % of the budget; the budget is nowhere near binding in the fixture, and it now has 509 ticks (8.5 s) of running time, not 600. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Carry-route feasibility (X3, D71; Layout's side only).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The Boarding ruling lengthens the decision-bearing carry in the reference derelict to about 21–28 tiles. content.content:
### D.5 Door leaf and passage

The door leaf formula (registry: `door_leaf_gap`) is defined as:

`gap(area) = floor_div(width_px × area, area_max)` · `leaf_w(area) = width_px − gap(area)` · `passes(F) ⇔ gap(area) ≥ F` · `area_pass_min(F) = ceil_div(F × area_max, width_px)` · `leaf_would_overlap(opening, area′, boxes) = ∃ L ∈ leaves(opening), ∃ f ∈ boxes : overlap(leaf_rect(L, area′), f)` (*Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:* `leaves(opening)` is one leaf for an interior door and **both** leaves of a mated hatch, each at its section's body-frame offset, with the opening's single `area_max`)

where `leaf_rect` for a doorway starting at `s` in an E-W wall whose footprint starts at `w` is: hinge `LOW`: `[s, s + leaf_w) × [w, w + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`; hinge `HIGH`: `[s + width_px − leaf_w, s + width_px) × [w, w + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`; a N-S wall swaps the axes. The leaf slides INTO the pocket on the hinge side, so the visible leaf stays anchored to the hinge end of the doorway and the gap opens from the other end. `leaf_w = 0` returns no rect (its `idx` stays reserved, D.9).

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width_px` | int (px) | 96 (the 96 × 96 door cell, art bible 8.2); lint `DOOR_WIDTH` | template | doorway width |
| `area` | int | `0 … area_max` | the Graph's opening state, read through `opening(edge_id)` (LY-10; published, the ask is closed); for a mated hatch, the shared OPENING's | the opening's current `area` (the Graph states 1/64 tile, LSG:72) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `area_max` | int | `> 0`, `≤ 128`; default 64 (`A_HOLE_MAX` 64, range 32–128, LSG:323 — cited as the scale reference) | template; for a mated hatch `min(a.area_max, b.area_max)` (LY-15) | full-open value; lint `DOOR_AREA_MAX` |
| `F` | int (px) | 16 across a doorway in an E-W wall, 8 across one in a N-S wall | the foot box 16 × 8 (PCI:103), supplied by Body | foot-box extent across the doorway |
| `hinge` | enum | `LOW`, `HIGH` | template (interior door); fixed `LOW` for a socket hatch (LY-9) | pocket side |
| `leaf_w`, `gap` | int (px) | `0 … width_px`; `gap` monotone non-decreasing in `area` | derived | leaf length and open length |

**Output Range:** `leaf_w`, `gap` in `[0, 96]`; the product `width_px × area` is at most `96 × 128 = 12,288`. At `area = 0` the leaf covers the doorway; at `area = area_max` there is no rect. Because the formula has no threshold, a binary jump `0 ↔ area_max` is binary by consequence and `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` is retired (LY-9).

**Example (`area_max` 64):** `area` 0 → `leaf_w` 96; 32 → 48; 64 → 0; 21 → `96 − floor_div(2016, 64) = 96 − 31 = 65`, `gap` 31; 10 → `gap` 15, 11 → `gap` 16. `area_pass_min(16) = ceil_div(1024, 96) = 11` (check: `gap(10) = 15 < 16`, `gap(11) = 16`) and `area_pass_min(8) = ceil_div(512, 96) = 6` (`gap(5) = 7`, `gap(6) = 9`). With `area_max` 128: `area_pass_min(16) = 22` (`gap(21) = 15`, `gap(22) = 16`) and `area_pass_min(8) = 11`. Leaf rect of `door_cryo_s` (E-W wall footprint `y` in `[384, 408)`, doorway `x` in `[240, 336)`, hinge `LOW`/west, `area_max` 64) at `area` 32: `[240, 288) × [384, 408)`, gap `[288, 336)`. **Close-safety:** closing from `area` 32 to 20 gives `leaf_w = 96 − floor_div(1920, 64) = 66`, leaf `[240, 306) × [384, 408)`; a foot box `[296, 312) × [384, 392)` overlaps it (`240 < 312`, `296 < 306`, `384 < 392`, `384 < 408`), so `leaf_would_overlap` is true and a PLAYER-origin close returns `OBSTRUCTED` (LY-11). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Mated-hatch example (the seam-straddling case):** the `fixture_airlock` weld of D.6 with `area_max` 64 (the minimum of 64 and 128): the opening's leaves are A's `[672, 696) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)` and B's `[696, 720) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)`. Closing from `area` 32 to 20 gives `leaf_w` 66, so both leaves reach `y` 306. The foot box `[696, 712) × [296, 304)` overlaps **only B's leaf** (`696 < 720`, `296 < 306`; against A's leaf `696 < 696` is false), so `leaf_would_overlap(opening, 20, [box])` is true; a check made against A's leaf alone would have returned false. (A box `[688, 704) × [296, 304)` straddling the seam overlaps both.) The (MVP) binary close tests the jump to `area` 0 the same way.

**Passage record (`door_passage`)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: `orientation` = `EW` for a door in an E-W wall, `NS` in a N-S wall. For a doorway starting at `s` in an E-W wall whose footprint starts at `w`: `sill_rect = [s, s + 96) × [w, w + 24)`; `open_extent_px = gap(area)` (0 when closed, 96 when `area = area_max`); `gap_rect`, hinge `LOW` = `[s + leaf_w, s + 96) × [w, w + 24)`, hinge `HIGH` = `[s, s + gap) × [w, w + 24)`; a N-S wall swaps the axes (`sill_rect = [w, w + 24) × [s, s + 96)`). `gap_rect` is NONE iff `open_extent_px = 0`, and equals `sill_rect` when `area = area_max`. The OUT convention is LY-12 (b)'s: every returned rect is the occupied span `(x0, y0, x1 − 1, y1 − 1)` (the half-open figures above are the stored form). The read returns NO passable flag: the caller compares `open_extent_px` with its foot extent `F` (`passes(F) ⇔ gap ≥ F`; `F` supplied by Body/Controller, PCI:103: 16 across an E-W doorway, 8 across a N-S one). **Mated hatch:** the opening's single `area_max = min(a, b)` and the fixed LOW hinge (LY-9, LY-15) apply; each section answers for its OWN leaf in its OWN section-local frame, and both answer the same `open_extent_px`. The read re-uses the leaf value `layout.doors` last projected (the same `leaf_w` that sizes the leaf rect), so collision, light and passage cannot disagree and `opening()` is not read a second time; an unknown opening reads as closed (the existing `opening_unknown` edge case), so `open_extent_px = 0`. It changes exactly when `leaf_version(section_id)` bumps (LY-12 d), so a reader's cache keyed on `version(section_id)` is correct (Horror HE-25 keys so). Cost: O(1) integer arithmetic, no `QueryBuffer`, safe in a P3 hook after `layout.doors` (`body.integrate` is `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]` and `horror.step` follows `body.integrate`, so a Horror run sees same-tick state).

**Worked values** (`door_cryo_s`, E-W, `s` 240, `w` 384, hinge LOW, `area_max` 64; `sill_rect` span (240, 384, 335, 407) in every row): `area` 0 → `open_extent_px` 0, `gap_rect` NONE; `area` 4 → `gap` floor_div(384, 64) = 6, LOW (330, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 245, 407); `area` 8 → 12, LOW (324, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 251, 407); `area` 11 → floor_div(1056, 64) = 16, LOW (320, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 255, 407); `area` 32 → 48, LOW (288, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 287, 407); `area` 64 → 96, `gap_rect` (240, 384, 335, 407). **N-S variant** (a harness-added door, as AC-52 adds `door_b`; `w` 384, `s` 240, footprint `x` in [384, 408), doorway `y` in [240, 336)): `sill_rect` span (384, 240, 407, 335); `area` 8 (12 px): LOW (384, 324, 407, 335), HIGH (384, 240, 407, 251); `area` 4 (6 px): LOW (384, 330, 407, 335), HIGH (384, 240, 407, 245). Against `F`: 6 px is passable across neither orientation, 12 px across N-S only (12 ≥ 8, 12 < 16), 16 px across both. `area_max` 128 with `area` 1 gives `open_extent_px = floor_div(96, 128) = 0`.

content.content:
### D.13 World tile ceiling and rect budget

The world ceiling formula is defined as:

`world_tiles = Σ V(room)` over rooms of the loaded set · `ERROR ⇔ world_tiles > TILES_WORLD_MVP` · `WARN ⇔ world_tiles × 100 ≥ TILES_WORLD_MVP × WORLD_TILES_WARN_PCT` · `rects(body) ≤ MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `V(room)` | int | 4 … 200 | D.3 | room volume |
| `TILES_WORLD_MVP` | int | 600 | Failure & Trail table data (FT:598) — a lint ceiling, not a Layout constant | world tile ceiling |
| `WORLD_TILES_WARN_PCT` | int (%) | 90 (80–95) | this GDD | WARN line (540) |
| `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` | int | 2,000 (1,000–4,000) | this GDD, sized to the Controller's performance criterion (PCI:1078) | rect budget of one body |

**Output Range:** lint verdicts `WORLD_TILES_NEAR_CEILING` (WARN) and `WORLD_TILES_OVER_CEILING` (ERROR); a build over the rect budget fails `can_build` with `CAPACITY`.

**Example (the registry's authored roster, `mvp_template_roster`; the earlier illustrative 502 is retired):** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `home_ship` `V` total 182 (5 rooms), `derelict_a` 118 (4 rooms), `derelict_b` 149 (5 rooms): the three ships total **449**, which is 74.8 % of 600; the always-dormant `pod_cabin` (`V` 4) makes **453** (75.5 %) if counted — the figure AC-100, AC-140 and the registry all use. Both pass, well below the 540 WARN line. Rects: about 250–400 unmerged across the three ship sections (the pod adds a handful) (planning estimate), the home-ship body about 90–150, against 2,000.

### D.22 Query cost model (planning arithmetic, not a rule)

The query cost model formula is defined as:

`cost(query) = t_call + cells × ( t_cell + rects_per_cell × t_dedup ) + t_merge(candidates) + candidates × t_test + N_dyn × t_bbox + t_merge_dyn(N_hit)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the dynamic leaf / variant list is not in the grid, so every query scans it and merges its hits into the key-ordered output; the earlier model omitted both terms)* and `tests_per_actor_tick = cells(swept_box) × rects_per_cell + sweep_tests` · one `solid_in` per actor per tick with the swept box `[px − 8 − v, px + 8 + v) × [py − v, py + 8 + v)` (half-open), `v = V_RUN`, then an analytic axis-separated sweep (never one query per 1-px step); the per-tick aggregate is `Σ over actors cost(solid_in) + Σ over Emitter and Lighting queries cost(rects_in)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier model counted AABB tests only and omitted the cell lookup, the de-duplication and merge of a rect that spans several cells, the call overhead, and every non-Body consumer.)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cells(swept_box)` | int | ≤ 4 at cell 48 | D.9 | grid cells touched |
| `rects_per_cell` | int | about 4 | planning estimate [UNV] | broadphase density |
| `sweep_tests` | int | about 16 | planning estimate [UNV] | analytic sweep against the candidate list |
| `N_dyn` | int | about 6 (MVP body; up to `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` 48 as a stress bound) | planning estimate [UNV] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | length of the body's dynamic leaf / variant list scanned by every query (bounding-box test each) |
| `t_bbox` | µs | about 0.5–1.5 | **[UNV]** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | one bounding-box reject test per dynamic entry (same order as `t_test`) |
| `t_merge_dyn(N_hit)` | µs | about 1 + 0.2 × `N_hit`, `N_hit` about 0–2 | **[UNV]** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | inserting the dynamic hits into the key-ordered output |
| per-test cost `t_test` | µs | about 0.5–1.5 | **[UNV]**, NOT SOURCEABLE (no GDScript cost data in the engine reference) | one AABB test *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| call overhead `t_call` | µs | about 1–3 | **[UNV]** | one GDScript call, buffer `clear()` and the 64-bit key column writes *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| cell lookup `t_cell` | µs | about 0.5–1 | **[UNV]** | one grid-cell index computation and read *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| de-dup `t_dedup` | µs | about 0.3–0.8 | **[UNV]** | one generation-stamp check per candidate (a rect spanning k cells is met k times) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| merge `t_merge(c)` | µs | about 1 + 0.2 × c | **[UNV]** | ordering the candidates by `rect_key` (insertion into the sorted output) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Emitter-sized query | box | 288 × 288 px (lamp radius `R_DRAW_MAX_PX` 144) → up to 7 × 7 = 49 cells at cell 48, about 100–200 candidate rects | planning estimate [UNV] | a `rects_in` call from the Emitter's static-layer rebuild or a segment test; amortised by the `static_version` cache (LY-12 d) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| actors per tick | int | 4 seats + the horror entities in range (about 6–8 in the MVP) | planning estimate | the aggregate-actor case *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Output Range:** about 32 tests plus the cell, de-dup, merge and call terms, about 0.028–0.072 ms per actor per tick from the static table (low: 1 + 6.8 + 4.2 + 16 = 28 µs; high: 3 + 16.8 + 4.2 + 48 = 72 µs, at 4 cells and 16 candidates), plus the dynamic terms at `N_dyn` 6 and `N_hit` 1 (3–9 µs scan plus 1.2 µs merge), so **about 0.033–0.082 ms, rounded to 0.03–0.08 ms** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier '0.04 to 0.08' did not follow from the table)* — above the Controller's budget of 0.05 ms P99 over 2,000 rects (PCI:1078) at the pessimistic end, which is why the pass lines are spike measurements (group K), not rules; the aggregate for 8 actors is then 0.26–0.66 ms of the 16.6 ms frame (**AC-164's aggregate line of at most 0.6 ms is the budget; AC-136's 0.05 ms P99 per actor is the target**, and the pessimistic end of the model exceeds the line, which is why group K is a spike) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and an Emitter-sized query is about 0.1–0.3 ms, paid only on a `static_version` change. ### D.21 Block size estimate

The block size formula is defined as:

`bytes ≈ 4 × ( 13·I + 10·K + 4·S + 3·B + 3 )` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the instance row is 13 ints, one more than before, because `template_hash` is split into `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash`)*

| `I` | int | 0 … live cap + tombstones | the block | instance rows (13 ints each; discarded rows stay as tombstones, LY-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `K` | int | `I − 1` at most per body | the block | weld rows (10 ints: ids, state, two 2-int times) |
| `S` | int | 0 … `8 × I` | the block | non-`FREE` socket rows (4 ints) |
| `B` | int | 1 … | the block | body rows incl. `DISSOLVED` (3 ints) |

**Output Range:** tens of bytes to tens of KB against `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` 32 MiB (REG:1915); excludes the template-id strings and the snapshot container overhead [UNV].

A long campaign with 24 live and 200 tombstoned sections, 200 weld rows, 400 socket rows and 208 bodies: `4 × (2,912 + 2,000 + 1,600 + 624 + 3) = 28,556` bytes (about 28 KB), still four orders of magnitude below the ceiling; `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` 65,536 raises a diagnostic long before. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

### D.6 Weld offset and the 24-grid closure

The weld offset formula (registry: `weld_offset`) is defined as:

`pos(socket) = (line_px, start_px)` for facing E or W, `(start_px, line_px)` for facing N or S · `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a − pos_b`, where **`a` is the survivor-side socket and `b` the absorbed-side socket, assigned by body (the body with the lower `body_id` survives, LY-16), never by argument order** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* · mate holds iff facings opposite ∧ `width_tiles` equal ∧ classes compatible ∧ lane multisets equal ∧ `¬overlap(rect_a, rect_b + offset_b − offset_a)` for every static-footprint pair (all static rects with all flags, each PLATE at its full footprint, plus room tile cells; LY-14) (`GEOM_OVERLAP`)

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset_a`, `offset_b` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid; `(0, 0)` at build (LY-25); may be negative after a detach re-base | the block | body-frame section origins |
| `pos_a`, `pos_b` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid (lint `GRID_24`); local `≥ 0` | template sockets | the socket reference point (LY-13) |
| `width_tiles` | int | 1 … 12 (`L_seam`, LSG:328 — cited) | template | equal for both sockets of a mate |

**Output Range:** `offset_b` on the 24-px grid. **`frame_shift_px` (attach)** `= offset_b − offset_b_old`, the position of the absorbed body's frame origin expressed in the host body's frame (`offset_b_old` is section b's offset inside its own body before the weld, `(0, 0)` for a freshly built single-section body, LY-25); every section of the absorbed body GAINS `frame_shift_px` (`new = old + frame_shift_px`). D.12's detach `frame_shift` has the same meaning mirrored (the position of the split-off body's new frame origin in the old frame; moved sections LOSE it), so one sentence serves Body for both. **24-grid closure (one line):** every input of the sum lies on the 24 grid (`GRID_24`-linted) and `offset_a` does by induction from `(0, 0)`, so `offset_b` does — a derived property, not an input constraint, and the reason `OFFSET_OFF_GRID` is unreachable and no socket phase is needed. After translation the two hull footprints abut: A facing E occupies `[line_a − 24, line_a)` in its normal axis and B facing W occupies `[line_b, line_b + 24)`, which lands at `[offset_a + line_a, offset_a + line_a + 24)`.

**Example:** home-ship airlock socket E-facing, `pos_a = (696, 240)`, `width_tiles` 2, `offset_a = (0, 0)`; derelict B socket W-facing, `pos_b = (120, 144)`, `width_tiles` 2: `offset_b = (0 + 696 − 120, 0 + 240 − 144) = (576, 96)` — 12 tiles by 2 tiles, on the 24 grid. B's W wall footprint local `[120, 144)` lands at body `[696, 720)`, abutting A's E wall `[672, 696)`; B's hatch local `y` `[144, 240)` lands at `[240, 336)`, in line with A's. `L_seam = 2`. For this attach `offset_b_old = (0, 0)`, so `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)`: the absorbed body's section 3 moves from `(0, 0)` to `(576, 96)` in the host frame, which is the same vector D.12's cut example returns when that seam is cut again. **Reversed-argument example** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: calling `attach_section(sock_b_w, sock_airlock_e, …)` — derelict B's socket first — still survives body 1 (the lower id, the home-ship), absorbs body 3, and returns the same `offset_b = (576, 96)` and `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)`; the roles `a`/`b` of the formula are the home-ship socket and B's socket in both calls. **`GEOM_OVERLAP` negative example:** a B bumper rect local `[96, 120) × [144, 192)` lands at body `[672, 696) × [240, 288)` and overlaps A's E wall `[672, 696) × [240, 336)` (`672 < 696`, `672 < 696`, `240 < 336`, `240 < 288`), so the verdict is `GEOM_OVERLAP`. A socket `start_px` of 150 never reaches this formula: it fails `GRID_24` at load.

### Feel Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No playtester reports seeing through a wall or door they could not walk through, or the reverse, across a full MVP session (Player Fantasy experience target X-2; mirrored by the same-tick door criterion in Acceptance Criteria group D).
- [ ] After one weld and one session, a playtester can walk to the seam and say which side was the original ship without prompting (X-1). Gate: this criterion is BLOCKED-ON the art-director's donor-wear commitment (OQ-25); the seam bead alone is symmetric and does not satisfy it. If OQ-25 is declined, X-1 is a Vertical Slice criterion, not MVP.
- [ ] A playtester who cut the graft can point to where it was in a later session (X-4).
- [ ] Asked "can you rearrange your ship?", playtesters do not ask for a build mode (X-3, MVP form); the fuller answer "no, but we choose what to weld on and cut off" is a Vertical Slice criterion, because one socket and one mate leave no choice of *what* to weld *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
- [ ] Protocol for every criterion above: at least 5 first-time playtesters, a scripted session, transcripts coded by two reviewers; X-1 passes at 4 of 5, X-2 at 0 of 5 reports, X-3 and X-4 at 4 of 5 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
- [ ] With a door blocked by a crewmate in the doorway and a door with no power in the same session, at least 4 of 5 playtesters correctly say which is which without being told, and none says "the door is broken" of the blocked one (AC-148). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; blocked on the Interaction / art-director cue, OQ-31)*

These are recorded, not hidden. None is a criterion; each has an owner in Open Questions.

- **Foot-box vertical placement — RESOLVED by Ship Body BDY-14 (registry `foot_box`).** The foot origin is the box's TOP row, centred in x: box `[pos.x − 8, pos.x + 8) × [pos.y, pos.y + 8)` (`FOOT_BOX_W` 16, `FOOT_BOX_H` 8), so the first legal row south of a wall `[y_0, y_0 + 24)` is `y_0 + 24` and the rest row north of one is `y_1 − 8`. Layout's criteria stay stated on rectangles and caller boxes (boundary-fixture criterion); only the Controller's PCI:103/447/651/908 'foot-centred' wording remains to refresh (Controller owner).
- **Contracts with neighbours that own the other half.** The restore order of `body.state`, `frame_shift_px` consumption by `BODY_TRANSFER`, the `body.integrate` `after:` order (registered by Ship Body BDY-8) and the Authoring lint hand-offs are untestable inside Layout (all those neighbours are now designed; the half each owns is tested in its own GDD); the host-body rule is Layout's and is tested (AC-150). Only Procedural Derelict Generation's contract is still provisional. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **Reference machines.** RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK are named (delegated ruling R12, OQ-2 closed); the spike pass lines of group K are pending spike measurement on them. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*

content.content:
### D.12 Detach re-base and components

The detach re-base formula (registry: `detach_rebase`) is defined as:

components of the ACTIVE `welds[]` forest minus the cut seam, enumerated in ascending `section_id` · `C_keep` = the component containing the body's `origin_section_id` (it keeps `body_id`) · `C_new` = the other component (it receives `body_id = next_body_id`, then `next_body_id += 1`) · `m = min(section_id) over C_new` · the new body's `origin_section_id = m` · `frame_shift = offset_old(m)` · `offset_new(s) = offset_old(s) − frame_shift` for `s ∈ C_new` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `origin_section_id = m` was unstated)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `welds[]` ACTIVE rows | list | forest (LY-14: every weld merges two bodies) | the block | the weld relation over sections |
| `origin_section_id` | int | a section id in the body | `bodies[]` | the body's frame anchor |
| `offset_old(s)` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid, may be negative | the block | body-frame offset before the cut |
| `frame_shift` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid | derived | returned so Body keeps the avatar's screen position (PIPE:694) — Body's concern |

**Output Range:** exactly two components (the forest argument); keep-side offsets unchanged; new offsets are differences of 24-grid values, so they stay on the 24 grid; dirty keys `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<kept>`, `BODY/<new>` and `SEC/<id>` for **every section whose socket state changed (both sections of the seam, the unmoved kept-side one included) and every moved section**; each of those sections also gets its `version` and `static_version` bumped (LY-12 d). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The LM3 return list is `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}` with `rects[]` exactly `detach_preview(seam_id).rects[]`, computed before the sockets change *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*

**Example:** home ship section 1 at `(0, 0)` on body 1 (`origin_section_id` 1); derelict B section 3 at `(576, 96)` welded to 1; a wing section 4 at `(1056, 96)` welded to 3. Cutting seam (1, 3): components `{1}` and `{3, 4}`; `{3, 4}` gets a new body from `next_body_id`; `m = 3`, `frame_shift = (576, 96)`; new offsets section 3 `(0, 0)`, section 4 `(480, 0)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Dirty keys: 2 `BODY` (kept body 1 and the new body) + 3 `SEC` (section 1, whose socket state changed although it did not move, and the moved sections 3 and 4) + 1 `S` = **6**, far under `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; the earlier count of 4 missed the kept body and the unmoved section 1, whose open leaf becomes a solid plate. The new body's `origin_section_id` is `m = 3`.

The worked values show each section answers for its own 24-px leaf: A's [672,696) and B's [696,720). They abut across the seam and share only the along-wall span, so they cannot coincide. A literal test would fail.
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'both sections give open_extent_px 48 and gap rects with identical along-wall spans (y 240..287 for hinge LOW) that abut at x = 696 after composing section_offset'.

The piece index for welds[]-derived pieces (bead, plate, cap) is undefined, as is the class_rank-1 tie-break. The ruling was 'name whatever you need yourself', so the value should not stay open. findings.section: LY-16 / D.6 host rule vs Modular Ship Assembly MSA-11
findings.finding: Layout picks the surviving body as the lower body_id. Assembly MSA-11 picks the HOME-kind side. They agree only while the home body holds the lowest id. Layout never persists kind, so it cannot check this, and Layout's text never cites MSA-11. If the invariant breaks, MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT fires and is release-fatal.
findings.fix: State the invariant in LY-16 and LY-25: LM1 builds the home ship's section first, so its body_id is the lowest. Add an AC (extending AC-150) that a world built in reversed order trips MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT in the Assembly stub, and cite MSA-11.

findings.section: LY-29 reason sets / LM1 validate / Edge Cases (ids)
findings.finding: The next_body_id and next_room_id 2^31-1 bounds exist only in AC-176 and an Edge Case. The LM1 can_build and LM3 can_detach rule text covers only next_section_id <= 2^20-1 and MAX_BODIES. The AC-176 oracle has no rule behind it.
findings.fix: Add 'next_body_id <= 2^31 - 2' to can_detach and 'next_room_id + template rooms <= 2^31 - 1' to can_build in LY-29 and the LM1/LM3 validate cells.

The authored roster pair is (696,384) (registry mvp_template_roster, MSA-11). A reader or implementer takes (576,96) as the authored MVP value. Only OQ note L1785 explains the difference.

findings.finding: AC-11 'no k, s, field_h or zoom value is an input or constant' is a scan for one-letter tokens, so it is untestable as a source scan. The Game Feel line 'No reviewer uses the words invisible wall...' has an unbounded population.
findings.fix: AC-11: scan for the named identifiers k_eff, zoom_step, field_h and any Pipeline import in the Layout module, plus the existing behavioural half (results identical across the zoom ladder). Game Feel: bind to the AC-135 playtest (at least 5 playtesters, transcripts coded by two reviewers, zero uses).

findings.fix: Rewrite as: with all other blocks held fixed, state_hash(PERSIST, T) changes if and only if layout_hash changes.

data.summary:

Both blockers from the third review are resolved. D.10 now matches the kernel's ratified H64: SHA-256 prefix via HashingContext, kernel TLV block form, no byte loop, and layout_hash equals the kernel's block_hash. The kernel publishes that read, and the Save/Load block_state_hash agrees. AC-37 now matches the LY-7 hull-port row. The crisis-cut entombment item (OQ-35) is also closed, and Ship Body has the matching BDY-24(iii) and its ACs.

I re-checked the values this pass added or changed, and they hold. The checks that matched:
- D.5 passage worked values: gap, LOW/HIGH rects, N-S variant and the area_max 128 case.

14 RECOMMENDED and 2 NICE findings remain. About half carry over from the previous review and were not fixed by the cross-GDD pass. The main ones:
